title: pH definition

items.label: pH
items.meaning: negative base-10 logarithm of the hydronium ion concentration (unitless)

items.label: [H_3O^+]
items.meaning: molar concentration of hydronium ion (mol/L)

caution: H+(aq) and H3O+(aq) are used interchangeably; H3O+ is preferred, but H+(aq) is also accepted on the AP Exam.

title: pKw, pH and pOH at 25°C

items.label: pK_w
items.meaning: negative base-10 logarithm of K_w; equals 14.0 at 25°C (unitless)

items.label: pH
items.meaning: -log[H3O+] (unitless)

items.label: pOH
items.meaning: -log[OH-] (unitless)

caution: This holds at 25°C only. K_w depends on temperature, so pH + pOH and the pH of neutral water differ from 14 and 7.0 at other temperatures.

title: pOH definition

items.label: pOH
items.meaning: negative base-10 logarithm of the hydroxide ion concentration (unitless)

items.label: [OH^-]
items.meaning: molar concentration of hydroxide ion (mol/L)

caution: For a strong base, [OH-] gives pOH. Convert to pH (pH = 14 - pOH at 25°C) before reporting pH.

title: Water autoionization constant, Kw

items.label: K_w
items.meaning: equilibrium constant for the autoionization of water (unitless)

items.label: [H_3O^+]
items.meaning: molar concentration of hydronium ion (mol/L)

items.label: [OH^-]
items.meaning: molar concentration of hydroxide ion (mol/L)

caution: The value 1.0 × 10^-14 applies at 25°C only. K_w is temperature dependent.
ced_evidence: 8.1.A.2 Water autoionizes with an equilibrium constant Kw. EQN: Kw = [H3O+][OH−] = 1.0 × 10−14 at 25°C

title: Acid ionization constant, Ka

items.label: K_a
items.meaning: acid ionization (equilibrium) constant of the weak acid (unitless)

items.label: [H_3O^+]
items.meaning: equilibrium molar concentration of hydronium ion (mol/L)

items.label: [A^-]
items.meaning: equilibrium molar concentration of the conjugate base (mol/L)

items.label: [HA]
items.meaning: equilibrium molar concentration of the un-ionized weak acid (mol/L)

caution: Concentrations are equilibrium values. For a weak acid, [HA] at equilibrium is nearly the initial acid concentration, since only a small percentage ionizes.

title: Conjugate pair: Ka, Kb and Kw

items.label: K_w
items.meaning: water autoionization constant (unitless); 1.0 × 10^-14 at 25°C

items.label: K_a
items.meaning: acid ionization constant of the acid member of the conjugate pair (unitless)

items.label: K_b
items.meaning: base ionization constant of the conjugate base member of the same pair (unitless)

caution: K_a and K_b must belong to the same conjugate acid-base pair. The equivalent form is pK_w = pK_a + pK_b.
ced_evidence: 8.3.A.6 For any conjugate acid-base pair … Kw = Ka × Kb

items.label: pK_a
items.meaning: negative base-10 logarithm of the acid ionization constant (unitless)

items.label: K_a
items.meaning: acid ionization constant (unitless)

items.label: pK_b
items.meaning: negative base-10 logarithm of the base ionization constant (unitless)

items.label: K_b
items.meaning: base ionization constant (unitless)
